h1: Where to drink this weekend in Bengaluru: stout
title: Stout in Bengaluru this weekend | Craft Beer School
desc: Six Bengaluru brewpubs and taprooms with a stout on their list, Indian dishes to pair and a plan for a cool December evening.
teaser: Dry, roasty and easier than it looks. Six places across Bengaluru list a stout this weekend.
standfirst: Bengaluru brews more stouts than most Indian cities, from nitro pours to coffee stouts. Here are six places to try one and a sensible way to plan the evening.
sections: A dry stout drinks lighter than its colour

The Irish dry stout is the one most people picture. It is lighter than it looks. Most are around 4 to 4.5 percent alcohol, with the body of a bitter rather than a strong ale. The black colour and sharp coffee bite come from roasted barley, unmalted grain roasted until it is nearly charred.

Look for black coffee without the milk, a firm bitterness and a quick, dry finish. Nothing should taste sweet or heavy. Serve it at 6 to 9 °C in a nonic pint. Cooler December evenings in Bengaluru suit it well. Our Irish dry stout style page has the full profile. The dry stout guide covers the brewing side.
Six Bengaluru stouts worth a phone call

All six below are confirmed as open in our directory. Not every one is a dry stout, which makes comparing them more fun. Beer lists come from our brewery directory, last checked September 2026. Taps rotate, so call ahead before you set out.

  • Toit, Indiranagar. Nitro Stout. Toit opened here in 2010. Basmati Blonde and a Hefeweizen are also listed.
  • The Biere Club, Richmond Town / Lavelle Road. Coffee Stout. Open since 2011, it also lists an English Pale Ale and a seasonal Lychee Basil Blonde.
  • Arbor Brewing Company, Ashok Nagar / MG Road. Michael Faricy Stout. Open since 2012, with Bangalore Bliss and Mango Maibock on the list.
  • Geist Brewing Co. Hennur, Hennur / Thanisandra. Geist Stouter Space at this taproom, alongside Geist James Blond and Geist Kamacitra.
  • ICB Indian Craft Brewery, Nagawara. Rowdy Stout. Opened in December 2024, it also lists Wit Maga and Happyweizen.
  • Ironhill Bengaluru, Marathahalli. Sinnerman Stout, with L.O.S.T. Lager and Wonderland and Wheat. The Ironhill group opened this one in 2021.
Roasted barley is a small share of a big flavour

On brew day, roasted barley usually makes up only around a tenth of a dry stout's grist. The rest is mostly pale malt. That small share does almost all the work on colour and roast, which is why brewers weigh it carefully. Push it much higher and the beer turns ashy and harsh instead of crisp.

Keep that in mind as you taste. A dry stout should feel balanced on the roast. A coffee stout like the one at The Biere Club adds coffee on top, so expect it to taste rounder. A nitro pour, like Toit's, softens the roast further with fine bubbles and a thick, creamy head. Most people can tell these apart on the first sip. Describing why is the skill our tasting guide starts you on.
What to eat with a stout

A dry stout is a quiet beer at the table, which is why it suits Indian food.

  • Chana masala with kulcha. Roasted cumin and the sourness of amchur play off the coffee notes. The dry finish keeps the meal from feeling heavy.
  • Vada pav. The roast matches the dry garlic chutney. The light body does not weigh down a fried snack.
  • Chocolate barfi. A bitter, roasty beer is a good counterweight to a sweet cocoa barfi, the way black coffee follows dessert.

Our guide to Indian food and beer pairing explains why these combinations work.
Plan by part of the city

For a central evening, The Biere Club in Richmond Town / Lavelle Road and Arbor in Ashok Nagar / MG Road are close neighbours. Add Toit in Indiranagar if you want a nitro stout as the third. In the north, Geist in Hennur / Thanisandra and ICB in Nagawara pair well.

Ask for tasters rather than pints. Two or three small pours across two stops will tell you plenty. Start with the dry or nitro stout and save the coffee stout for last, because its extra flavour will drown out a lighter beer tasted after it. Drink water with each round and eat something everywhere you stop. Take a cab or the metro home. Never drive after drinking.
Open the Irish dry stout style page and read the look and aroma notes before you go. Then call your first stop, check the stout is pouring and taste it against the description.
faqs: What temperature should stout be served at?
Irish dry stout is best at 6 to 9 °C. Served too cold, the roast and coffee notes go quiet.
Is a coffee stout the same as a dry stout?
No. A coffee stout adds coffee to a stout base, so it tastes rounder. A dry stout gets its coffee-like bite from roasted barley alone.
Will every venue have its stout on tap?
Not always. Taps rotate, so call ahead before you set out.
